question: How soon can ovulation return after an abortion procedure?

options.A: Only when the first normal period ends
options.B: After 6 months have passed
options.C: Within 10 to 14 days
options.D: After exactly 4 to 6 weeks

explanation: Ovulation often resumes very quickly after pregnancy termination, sometimes within two weeks, meaning a new pregnancy is possible before normal menstruation returns. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of an action plan during a project?

options.A: To raise funds from international organizations after the event
options.B: To change the objectives after the project has already started
options.C: To outline who is responsible for each task, the timeline, and required resources
options.D: To grade community members based on their health test scores

explanation: An action plan keeps everyone organized. It clearly shows who is doing what, when they are doing it, and what tools they need.

question: Where does the scrub nurse position themselves during an operation?

options.A: Within the sterile field
options.B: Outside the sterile zone managing room records
options.C: In the recovery ward receiving incoming patients
options.D: At the patient's head near the anaesthetic machine

explanation: The scrub nurse wears sterile personal protective gear and stands right inside the sterile zone, ready to pass tools to the surgeon.

question: You check a new mother's uterus and find it feels soft and boggy instead of firm. What should you do first?

options.A: Encourage her to walk in the hallway
options.B: Apply an ice pack to the perineum
options.C: Gentle fundal massage to help it contract
options.D: Give her a routine oral laxative

explanation: A soft or 'boggy' uterus needs a gentle massage to firm up and stop heavy bleeding. You are keeping her safe!

question: A doctor looks at a scan that cuts the body horizontally into upper and lower parts. Which plane is this?

options.A: Frontal plane
options.B: Midsagittal plane
options.C: Transverse plane
options.D: Sagittal plane

explanation: You're doing great! A transverse plane cuts across the body horizontally, giving us upper (superior) and lower (inferior) views. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which drug history is most important for a nurse to check before a patient has a lumbar puncture?

options.A: Multivitamins
options.B: Antacids
options.C: Antihistamines
options.D: Anticoagulants

explanation: Spot on! Blood thinners (anticoagulants) raise the risk of dangerous bleeding around the spine.

question: Which factor is primarily responsible for urge faecal incontinence?

options.A: Excessive production of stomach acid
options.B: Weakened sphincters unable to hold back a strong bowel urge
options.C: Permanent blockage of the upper gastrointestinal tract
options.D: Complete absence of the large intestine

explanation: In urge incontinence, the patient perceives the need to defecate, but weak muscles cannot keep the stool contained long enough to reach a toilet. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why do vitamin and mineral shortages happen so easily in people living with HIV?

options.A: Due to poor intake, malabsorption, and inflammation
options.B: Because the virus uses up all carbohydrates
options.C: Because antiretroviral drugs destroy vitamins instantly
options.D: Because they drink too much clean water

explanation: Spot on! Gut inflammation and eating less food mean the body struggles to absorb the vital nutrients it needs.

question: What main factor sets gender-based violence apart from other forms of violence?

options.A: It is directed against someone based on gender roles and inequalities
options.B: It only occurs within marriage and domestic settings
options.C: It is exclusively perpetrated by adult males against adult females
options.D: It involves physical assault without any psychological harm

explanation: You've got this! GBV stems from unequal power balances and societal expectations tied to gender. Recognizing this helps us look beyond just the physical acts.

question: What is the main purpose of a soft diet?

options.A: To reduce chewing and digestion effort
options.B: To provide only liquid nutrients
options.C: To completely eliminate the need for teeth
options.D: To restrict all protein and fat intake

explanation: A soft diet is designed to be easy on the mouth, teeth, and stomach by requiring less mechanical chewing and digestive work. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T002#GNS227_U6_T002_h1)

question: What is the basic working unit of the human kidney?

options.A: The nephron
options.B: The loop of Henle
options.C: The renal pelvis
options.D: The ureter

explanation: Great job! The nephron is the tiny but mighty unit inside your kidneys that filters your blood and makes urine. You've got this!

question: What is the main purpose of the Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale (RASS) in the ICU?

options.A: To measure the depth of sedation or level of agitation in a patient
options.B: To calculate the exact dosage of intravenous pain medication needed
options.C: To assess the risk of pressure ulcer formation over bony prominences
options.D: To evaluate how well the lungs are exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide

explanation: The RASS score helps the whole healthcare team figure out if a patient is resting peacefully, too sleepy, or too restless.

question: How should you apply antiseptic skin prep solution to a patient's surgical site?

options.A: In a random zig-zag pattern across the entire torso and limbs
options.B: Starting at the incision site and moving outward in circles
options.C: Starting at the outer edges and scrubbing inward to the center
options.D: Using a back-and-forth motion right over the planned incision

explanation: Always move from clean to dirty! Starting at the incision and working outward ensures you don't drag skin bacteria into the clean cut.

question: What is the absolute first thing to check and manage when a patient is brought in with a suspected drug overdose?

options.A: Drawing blood for lab tests
options.B: Finding out the exact name of the drug taken
options.C: Administering activated charcoal orally
options.D: Securing the airway, breathing, and circulation

explanation: You've got this! Always remember the ABCs (Airway, Breathing, Circulation) come first in any emergency. We keep the patient alive and breathing before we worry about detective work or giving specific medications.

question: What is the main problem that causes most cases of peripheral arterial disease (PAD)?

options.A: Deep veins staying stretched out permanently
options.B: Bacterial toxins destroying tiny capillaries
options.C: Tiny lymphatic tubes suddenly bursting
options.D: Fatty plaque building up and narrowing the arteries

explanation: That process is called atherosclerosis! Fat and cholesterol build up inside the arteries, making the pathway narrow so it's harder for oxygen-rich blood to reach the legs.

question: What blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the placenta back to the fetus?

options.A: Umbilical vein
options.B: Ductus venosus
options.C: Spiral endometrial artery
options.D: Umbilical artery

explanation: The umbilical vein is responsible for carrying freshly oxygenated and nutrient-rich blood from the placental villi back to the fetal circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h1)

question: What is the recommended angle for lifting the head of the bed for a patient on a mechanical ventilator?

options.A: 30 to 45 degrees
options.B: 0 to 15 degrees
options.C: 60 to 75 degrees
options.D: 90 degrees sitting upright

explanation: Keeping the bed raised between 30 and 45 degrees uses gravity to help stop spit or stomach juices from sliding down into the lungs.

question: A young adult is admitted after taking too many sleeping pills on purpose. They are now fully awake and stable. What is your most important immediate nursing action?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately with a prescription for vitamins.
options.B: Initiate strict suicide precautions and ensure constant observation.
options.C: Scold the patient regarding the dangers of taking medication.
options.D: Restrict all family members from visiting to maintain hospital quiet.

explanation: Just because they look physically stable doesn't mean the emotional crisis is over. Safety first—keep them under close watch and arrange mental health support right away.

question: A patient scheduled for morning surgery admits to eating a small piece of yam an hour ago. What should you do right away?

options.A: Document the meal in the chart and proceed with sending the patient to theatre.
options.B: Ask the patient to drink a large glass of water to clear the esophagus.
options.C: Administer an emetic medication to help the patient vomit the food quickly.
options.D: Notify the surgical and anesthesia team immediately regarding the food intake.

explanation: Eating breaks the NPO rule and can be dangerous during anesthesia. Always alert the surgical and anesthesia team right away so they can decide the next steps.

question: Why is a multi-sectoral approach necessary when managing cases of gender-based violence?

options.A: Because survivors need medical, legal, social, and psychological support
options.B: Because hospitals cannot provide medicines without a court order
options.C: Because nurses are legally forbidden from talking to police officers
options.D: Because social workers make more money than nurses do

explanation: Comprehensive recovery requires collaboration across health, legal, social, and security sectors. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h7)

question: How can untreated mental health issues like depression increase a person's risk of drug abuse?

options.A: They automatically cure physical pain and prevent addiction
options.B: They guarantee the person will never touch alcohol or drugs
options.C: They may use substances to self-medicate and numb emotional pain
options.D: They stop the brain from absorbing any psychoactive compounds

explanation: When people are hurting emotionally and lack mental health support, they sometimes turn to drugs or alcohol just to find relief.

question: What happens if a patient starts eating a lot of fiber but forgets to drink enough water?

options.A: The patient will immediately develop severe watery diarrhea
options.B: Constipation can actually worsen because stool becomes dry and bulky
options.C: Kidney function will fail due to excess nutrient absorption
options.D: Fiber will pass through the body completely unchanged

explanation: Remember: fiber acts like a sponge! Without water, it cannot swell properly and will just form a hard, difficult lump in the gut.

question: Which symptom should immediately tell a nurse a pregnant woman might have a hypertensive disorder?

options.A: Cravings for non-food items
options.B: Mild itching over the abdomen
options.C: Persistent headache and blurred vision
options.D: Frequent urination during the night

explanation: Headaches and changes in vision are classic red flags for pre-eclampsia. Always check her blood pressure and urinalysis right away!

question: Why is newborn screening so important for babies with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: It prevents the spleen from ever being damaged by blocked blood vessels
options.B: It stops red blood cells from ever changing into a crescent shape
options.C: It allows early penicillin prophylaxis and vaccination before severe infections occur
options.D: It cures the genetic mutation completely before symptoms start to show

explanation: Early detection saves lives! Finding the condition early lets doctors start daily penicillin and special vaccines right away, protecting the baby from dangerous infections.

question: Why do doctors need specific serological tests in addition to routine liver enzyme tests?

options.A: Routine enzymes cannot detect jaundice, whereas serological tests measure skin pigment
options.B: Liver enzymes show that injury is happening, but serological tests identify the exact viral cause
options.C: Serological tests are the only way to measure how much urine the patient is producing daily
options.D: Blood enzymes only work for Hepatitis A, requiring serological tests for all other diseases

explanation: Spot on! Routine liver tests tell us the liver is angry and inflamed, but serological blood tests act like detectives to tell us *which* specific virus started the fire.

question: Why do hospitals look at medication errors as system problems rather than just blaming the individual nurse?

options.A: Because doctors are legally responsible for every single pill a nurse hands out
options.B: Because regulatory agencies do not hold individual nurses accountable for errors
options.C: Because modern hospital computers prevent human nurses from making any wrong choices
options.D: Because poor workflows, fatigue, and confusing labels often set workers up for mistakes

explanation: Mistakes often happen because of tired shifts, busy wards, or confusing drug packaging. Fixing the workplace system keeps everyone safer, rather than just pointing fingers!

question: What does a molding score of +++ mean when you do a vaginal examination during labour?

options.A: Normal, loose separation of the baby's cranial bones
options.B: Premature fusion of the skull bones occurring years before birth
options.C: Total absence of the fetal head in the birth canal
options.D: Severe overlapping of fetal skull bones that cannot be separated

explanation: When you see +++, it means the baby's skull bones are overlapping tightly and can't be pushed apart. This is a red flag that the baby might be having a hard time passing through the pelvis.

question: Which of these is NOT part of a standard nursing check before a vasectomy?

options.A: Scheduling a mandatory prostate biopsy
options.B: Checking for active local skin infections
options.C: Screening for permanent reproductive intent
options.D: Evaluating bleeding history and anticoagulant use

explanation: That's right! A prostate biopsy checks for cancer and has nothing to do with routine preparation for a vasectomy.

question: What is the primary role of the Reticular Activating System (RAS) in the brain stem?

options.A: Processing visual images from the eyes
options.B: Controlling fine motor coordination
options.C: Maintaining wakefulness and alertness
options.D: Regulating resting heart rate

explanation: The RAS is like your brain's alarm clock! It keeps you awake, alert, and responsive to everything happening around you.

question: Why must nurses regularly check the vision of a patient who has a pituitary tumor?

options.A: Swelling from fluid retention causes temporary double vision.
options.B: High prolactin levels directly burn out the retina and nerve endings.
options.C: Lacking growth hormone makes the eyes unable to focus on close things.
options.D: Growing tumors can press against the optic nerves and cause gradual blindness.

explanation: Because the pituitary lives right below the optic chiasm, any tumor that starts expanding upward will threaten the patient's eyesight first. Regular checks catch this early!

question: What is a major safety worry for a patient who has lost feeling (protective sensation) in their arms or legs?

options.A: Rapid muscle hypertrophy
options.B: Excessive verbal outbursts
options.C: Sudden loss of hearing
options.D: Burns and pressure injuries

explanation: When patients can't feel hot, cold, or pressure, they won't pull away from a hot stove or shift their weight, leaving their skin wide open to quiet injuries and sores.

question: At what point in an illness can a patient usually start receiving palliative care?

options.A: Only during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.B: At the time of a serious illness diagnosis
options.C: Only when admitted to a dedicated hospice facility
options.D: After all curative treatments have completely failed

explanation: You don't have to wait until the end! Palliative care is meant to start early alongside other treatments to keep the patient as comfortable as possible.

question: Why would a person die from a minor infection if they had no inflammatory response?

options.A: The liver would immediately stop producing essential proteins
options.B: Blood pressure would drop too low to sustain life
options.C: The body could not isolate and destroy invading germs
options.D: Red blood cells would stop carrying oxygen to tissues

explanation: Inflammation is the critical defense mechanism that walls off and eliminates harmful agents in the body. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T1#GNS123_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why must a nurse stay at the bedside until the patient swallows all their medications?

options.A: To record the exact second the patient stops drinking water
options.B: To collect payment for the hospital prescription fees
options.C: To make sure the water cup is returned clean to the medication room
options.D: To confirm the patient actually takes the drugs and does not hide them

explanation: Staying at the bedside ensures compliance and safety, preventing patients from pocketing pills or missing doses. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h5)

question: What does an electroencephalogram (EEG) actually measure in a sick patient?

options.A: Pressure inside the cranial vault
options.B: Oxygen saturation in brain tissue
options.C: Electrical activity of the brain
options.D: Blood flow through the carotid arteries

explanation: Think of an EEG as a way to listen in on the brain's electrical chatter to spot things like seizures or abnormal brain wave patterns.

question: At what cervical dilation does the active phase of normal labor officially start on a partograph?

options.A: 8 centimeters
options.B: 10 centimeters
options.C: 1 centimeter
options.D: 4 centimeters

explanation: 4 centimeters is your magic marker! That is where the active phase of labor officially begins on the partograph.

question: What is the primary movement that pushes food down the esophagus?

options.A: Emulsification
options.B: Peristalsis
options.C: Segmentation
options.D: Mastication

explanation: Peristalsis involves wave-like muscular contractions that propel food smoothly through the digestive tract. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which suture separates the forehead bone (frontal bone) from the two top side bones (parietal bones)?

options.A: Sagittal suture
options.B: Coronal suture
options.C: Lambdoid suture
options.D: Metopic suture

explanation: You've got this! The coronal suture runs side to side across the skull like a crown, sitting right between the frontal and parietal bones.

question: In nursing, we say 'if it is not documented, it never happened.' What does this mean for patient education?

options.A: Patients completely forget everything the moment they leave the ward
options.B: Hospitals will not pay nurses for talking to patients
options.C: Doctors are the only staff allowed to speak about prescriptions
options.D: Verbal teaching has no legal proof without a written note in the chart

explanation: Documentation protects both you and the patient by providing legal proof that education actually took place. Always chart your care!

question: What is a major financial reason that pushes struggling families to marry off young daughters?

options.A: Requirement for agricultural labor grants
options.B: High cost of maintaining female education
options.C: Mandatory government marriage taxes
options.D: Desire to reduce household financial burdens

explanation: Extreme poverty forces some families to marry off young daughters simply to have one less mouth to feed. It's a tough reality, but understanding it helps us care better as nurses.

question: Why is it so important to document a drug reaction in the notes and tell the patient about it?

options.A: To prevent the patient from receiving the same dangerous drug in the future
options.B: To satisfy legal insurance requirements for the nursing council
options.C: To prove to the doctor that the nurse made the correct diagnosis
options.D: To make sure the hospital pharmacy gets paid for the wasted medication

explanation: Clear records and patient education protect them from getting that same harmful drug again in future hospital visits.

question: Which of these is NOT safe for staff working in the TSSU decontamination zone?

options.A: Putting on face shields and eye protection
options.B: Wearing waterproof protective aprons
options.C: Wearing open-toed sandals for comfort
options.D: Using heavy-duty utility gloves

explanation: Great catch! Open-toed shoes leave your feet exposed to falling sharps and dirty splashes. Always wear closed, protective shoes in the wash area!

question: Which common side effect of opioids do patients almost NEVER develop a tolerance to?

options.A: Nausea
options.B: Constipation
options.C: Euphoria
options.D: Sedation

explanation: While patients get used to the sleepiness and dizziness from opioids, the bowels stay slow. Always plan for laxatives!

question: How do bronchodilators help a patient who is struggling to breathe?

options.A: By increasing the total volume of red blood cells
options.B: By relaxing the smooth muscles around the airways
options.C: By removing excess fluid from the lung tissues
options.D: By killing bacterial infections in the alveoli

explanation: Bronchodilators open up tight, constricted breathing tubes so air can flow smoothly in and out of the lungs again.

question: What is the origin of most cancer-causing mutations?

options.A: Passed down exclusively through maternal bloodlines
options.B: Inherited directly from parents in every single diagnosed case
options.C: Acquired over a lifetime from environmental and lifestyle factors
options.D: Caused entirely by sudden bacterial infections in childhood

explanation: Most cancers arise from acquired mutations that build up over time due to exposure to external agents like tobacco, radiation, and unhealthy diets. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the main goal of conducting a financial audit in a hospital?

options.A: To punish individual bedside nurses for making minor clinical charting errors
options.B: To eliminate all patient care expenses across every hospital department
options.C: To verify the accuracy of financial records and ensure compliance with standards
options.D: To decide which physicians receive bonuses at the end of each month

explanation: Audits aren't witch hunts—they are routine checks to make sure financial records are honest, accurate, and following the rules.

question: Which urine collection method is best when a doctor suspects an infection and orders a urine culture?

options.A: First morning random specimen
options.B: Random afternoon specimen
options.C: Initial voided stream sample
options.D: Clean-catch midstream specimen

explanation: The clean-catch midstream method is a classic! By letting the first bit of urine wash away skin germs, we catch a sample that truly shows what's happening inside the bladder.

question: At what level does management happen in a hospital?

options.A: Only at the executive board room level
options.B: Exclusively within the hospital pharmacy department
options.C: At every level from charge nurse to director
options.D: Strictly during annual government audits

explanation: Management isn't just for bosses in suits! From frontline charge nurses managing the ward to senior directors, everyone plays a leadership role.

question: What is the main goal of community-wide public declarations to stop FGM?

options.A: Forcing traditional rulers to give up their titles
options.B: Getting direct cash grants from foreign donors
options.C: Removing social pressure by having families agree together to drop the practice
options.D: Registering all villagers into the national health insurance plan

explanation: Correct! Public declarations protect individual families from being ostracized by ensuring everyone agrees to stop cutting at the same time.

question: What does peripheral resistance refer to in the circulatory system?

options.A: Fluid loss through capillary pores
options.B: Friction of blood against vessel walls
options.C: The pumping strength of the left atrium
options.D: The speed of oxygen binding to hemoglobin

explanation: Peripheral resistance is the drag or friction blood experiences as it travels through the blood vessels. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T12#GNS111_U2_T12_h6)

question: Why is maintaining the cold chain so important in immunization programs?

options.A: To keep vaccines potent and effective until administration
options.B: To prevent the clinic refrigerator from overheating
options.C: To freeze liquid vaccines into solid blocks
options.D: To make the vaccines easier to draw into a syringe

explanation: Brilliant! Vaccines are delicate biological products. If they get too warm, they lose their power to protect children against diseases.

question: A client stopped taking her oral contraceptive pills because she kept forgetting daily doses. What is a great alternative to suggest?

options.A: Switching to a long-acting method like an implant or injection
options.B: Stopping all contraception permanently without alternatives
options.C: Taking three pills at once every Sunday morning
options.D: Relying entirely on calendar guessing without records

explanation: Long-acting reversible contraceptives (LARCs) like implants or injections take the stress out of daily pill-taking!

question: What is the primary physiological cause of fainting?

options.A: A sudden temporary drop in blood flow to the brain
options.B: An acute electrical storm in the brain tissue
options.C: A permanent blockage of the carotid arteries
options.D: A severe deficiency of potassium in the blood

explanation: Fainting happens when cerebral blood flow drops briefly, starving the brain of oxygen and glucose. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h1)

question: What is considered the single most effective measure to prevent the spread of germs?

options.A: Avoiding all outdoor activities
options.B: Wearing heavy lead aprons
options.C: Taking daily multivitamins
options.D: Regular hand hygiene

explanation: Handwashing and hand sanitizing remove transient microorganisms, drastically reducing the transmission of infectious agents. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is the main job of the vagina in the female body?

options.A: Producing female sex hormones
options.B: Storing eggs before fertilization
options.C: Filtering waste products from blood
options.D: Connecting the vulva to the cervix

explanation: You got this! The vagina is simply a muscular canal that acts as a direct passageway between the outside (vulva) and the uterus (via the cervix).

question: What kind of tumor grows into nearby tissues and travels to other parts of the body?

options.A: Benign tumor
options.B: Metaplastic lesion
options.C: Malignant tumor
options.D: Hyperplastic growth

explanation: Spot on! Malignant tumors are cancerous because they don't stay in one place—they can invade local tissues and travel through the blood or lymph to other parts of the body.

question: What specific condition does erythromycin eye ointment prevent in a newborn?

options.A: Congenital cataracts from viral infections
options.B: Dry eyes from forgetting to blink
options.C: Blinding eye infections from maternal sexually transmitted bugs
options.D: Blocked tear ducts from narrow passages

explanation: It's a standard protective step given right after birth to shield the baby's eyes from infections like gonorrhea or chlamydia picked up in the birth canal.

question: A patient is scheduled for a hysterosalpingography (HSG). What is the most important preparatory action for the nurse to take?

options.A: Administer a cleansing enema to empty the entire colon
options.B: Explain the procedure steps and what kind of cramping sensation to expect
options.C: Instruct the patient to fast from solid food for twenty-four hours
options.D: Place an indwelling urinary catheter before the imaging begins

explanation: Preparation is all about calming nerves! Explaining what will happen and warning them about mild period-like cramps helps the patient feel safe and ready.

question: Which symptom helps tell a yeast infection apart from trichomoniasis?

options.A: A painless firm chancre on the external labia
options.B: Frothy, yellow-green discharge with a strong, fishy smell
options.C: Painful, fluid-filled vesicles that rupture into open ulcers
options.D: Thick, white, cottage-cheese-like discharge with no foul odor

explanation: Yeast infections (candidiasis) usually bring thick, white discharge and intense itching, unlike the frothy, foul-smelling discharge of trichomoniasis.

question: A young female patient has lower abdominal pain and cries out in severe pain when the nurse moves her cervix during a pelvic exam. What is the most likely condition?

options.A: Uterine fibroids
options.B: Primary dysmenorrhea
options.C: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome
options.D: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease

explanation: That intense pain when moving the cervix is called 'cervical motion tenderness' (or a positive chandelier sign), and it's a classic red flag for PID.

question: A farmer who sprays crops without protection starts feeling dizzy and shaky. What is the likely cause?

options.A: Physical hazard from extreme heat
options.B: Chemical hazard from pesticides
options.C: Ergonomic hazard from heavy lifting
options.D: Biological hazard from soil bacteria

explanation: Pesticides are powerful chemicals that can easily enter the body during spraying and trigger toxic symptoms like dizziness and tremors.

question: Which level of cleaning is practically never done inside a regular home care setting?

options.A: Sterilization
options.B: Disinfection
options.C: Cleaning
options.D: Sanitization

explanation: Spot on! Sterilization destroys every single spore and needs heavy hospital equipment like autoclaves—definitely not something you do in a living room.

question: You notice some insulin vials have been sitting on a warm desk for hours. What should you do?

options.A: Dilute the warm insulin with sterile water to restore its cold temperature
options.B: Consult the pharmacy or discard the compromised vials according to policy
options.C: Return them immediately to the patient refrigerator without checking
options.D: Administer them quickly before the expiration date arrives next month

explanation: You nailed it. Insulin is sensitive to heat and loses its potency when left out. Always check with pharmacy or follow safety rules rather than risking a patient's dose.

question: Why do modern syringe drivers have security locks on their control panels?

options.A: To prevent the battery from falling out during transport
options.B: To automatically lock the infusion line if air bubbles appear
options.C: To prevent accidental changes to the rate by visitors or patients
options.D: To keep the internal clock set to the correct local time zone

explanation: Spot on! Security locks ensure that inquisitive fingers or accidental bumps don't change the prescribed medication speed.

question: At what point in the procedure should you release the tourniquet?

options.A: Immediately after the first blood tube is filled
options.B: Before pulling the needle out of the vein
options.C: Before inserting the needle into the skin
options.D: After applying the adhesive bandage to the arm

explanation: Remember to release the tourniquet before taking the needle out. This stops extra blood from leaking out and prevents a nasty bruise from forming.

question: What makes a clinic truly "youth-friendly" when it comes to reproductive health?

options.A: Programs that focus solely on treating severe physical trauma injuries
options.B: Medical facilities that treat only patients under twelve years of age
options.C: Clinics that operate exclusively during late night hours on weekends
options.D: Services that offer confidential, non-judgmental care tailored to teenagers

explanation: Youth-friendly clinics win teens' trust by keeping their business private, listening without scolding, and treating them with absolute respect.

question: A patient complains of constant dizziness and trouble keeping their balance. Which part of the ear is likely involved?

options.A: External ear canal
options.B: Auditory ossicles
options.C: Tympanic membrane
options.D: Semicircular canals

explanation: The semicircular canals in your inner ear are your body's built-in spirit level. They track your head movements and help keep you balanced.

question: Why is it important for a clinical nurse to know the specific classification of a patient's FGM?

options.A: It reveals the exact religious sect that performed the procedure.
options.B: It helps determine the exact financial cost of surgical reconstruction.
options.C: It dictates the specific legal punishment for the family members involved.
options.D: It predicts the specific physical and psychological complications the patient may face.

explanation: Different types of FGM involve varying degrees of tissue removal and scarring, directly influencing clinical complications and care needs. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h1)

question: Clinic records show few malaria cases, but local medicine vendors report selling lots of malaria drugs daily. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Report the clinic staff to the ministry for failing to do their jobs
options.B: Use community-based data collection like household surveys to find the real disease burden
options.C: Assume the medicine vendors are lying and close down their shops
options.D: Conclude that malaria has been completely eradicated in that area

explanation: Not everyone goes to the government clinic first; many buy drugs across the counter. To find the true picture, nurses must look beyond clinic logbooks and talk to the community directly.

question: Which of these is a great example of a drug working without using a receptor?

options.A: An insulin molecule attaching to a muscle cell
options.B: An opioid binding to a brain pain receptor
options.C: A beta-blocker slowing down the heart rate
options.D: An osmotic laxative pulling water into the bowel
